summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, left lower extremity pain following frostbite and skin graft, and chronic pain management needs was admitted for pain control and possible UTI. She had recently been discharged from a shelter and lacked stable housing. She requested IV Dilaudid, but the medical team determined she could safely continue her home regimen of oral Dilaudid. Due to her refusal to accept oral medication and escalating distress, she chose to leave against medical advice. A urine test showed epithelial cells but no signs of active infection, so antibiotics were not given. Social work was consulted for housing support, but she declined to wait. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up recommended.
